# The Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, tucked into the margins of a library copy of *Wuthering Heights*. Marisol Chen found it while checking the book back in—*haworth is 40 miles from Thrushcross Grange, not 4, check your geography*—written in a small, careful hand, the pencil strokes so light they were almost apologetic.

She should have been annoyed. Pencilling in library books was vandalism, technically, even if it was erasable. Instead, she found herself holding the book open under the returns desk lamp, tilting the page, studying the handwriting. The letters were old-fashioned, looped and upright, the kind of cursive nobody under seventy used anymore.

She erased it. That was the rule. But she kept noticing them after that.

A biography of Captain Cook came back with a note about the tonnage of the *Endeavour*. A novel set in 1920s Dublin had its street names corrected, one by one.
